title: TransitLM: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Map-Free Transit Route Generation
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Traditional pipelines need costly map infrastructure and general LLMs hallucinate; ours generates valid outputs end-to-end from data alone.
layout: 3 panels: top traditional pipeline, bottom-left LLM, bottom-right ours; checkmarks/crosses
description: A three-paradigm comparison, with each panel in its own color. The top panel, red, is titled Traditional Methods. It shows four boxes joined by arrows: User Input, Map Data Retrieval, Routing Algorithm and Ranking. Beside them are a green check for industrially proven and red crosses for high costs and static configuration only. The bottom-left panel, blue, is General-purpose LLM. It shows a user query leading to an LLM output route in which an invalid station is marked by a dashed line and a crossed node. A Failure Modes box lists hallucinated stations, disconnected route and invalid boarding/alighting stations. The bottom-right panel, green, is TransitLM (Ours). It shows a user query leading to a valid LLM output route, with TransitData and TransitBench boxes feeding in through pre-train/fine-tune arrows. Green checks list the strengths. A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Three paradigms for transit route planning. Top: Traditional map-based pipeline. Bottom-left: General-purpose LLMs lack structural grounding, producing hallucinated stations, disconnected routes, and invalid boarding/alighting points. Bottom-right: TransitLM generates structurally valid, continuous routes end-to-end via implicit spatial grounding, without map infrastructure.
abstract: Public transit route planning traditionally depends on structured map infrastructure and complex routing engines, and no existing dataset supports training models to bypass this dependency. We present TransitLM, a large-scale dataset of nearly 13 million transit route planning records from four Chinese cities covering 120,845 stations and 13,666 lines, released as a continual pre-training corpus and benchmark data for three evaluation tasks with complementary metrics. Experiments show that an LLM trained on TransitLM produces structurally valid routes at high accuracy and implicitly grounds arbitrary GPS coordinates to appropriate stations without any explicit mapping. These results demonstrate that transit route planning can be learned entirely from data, enabling end-to-end, map-free route generation directly from origin-destination information. The dataset and benchmark are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/GD-ML/TransitLM, with evaluation code at https://github.com/HotTricker/TransitLM.
